hook.text: Carrageenan from red seaweed thickens your almond milk. But some scientists want it banned for gut damage.

buildup.text: Irish Moss (Chondrus crispus) has been used in food for centuries. Carrageenan is its extracted polysaccharide.

discovery.text: Three types exist: kappa sets firm gels, iota makes soft gels, lambda thickens without gelling. Each has a role.

twist.text: Degraded carrageenan (poligeenan) causes gut inflammation in animals. But food-grade carrageenan is a different molecule.

climax.text: Organic standards briefly considered banning it. Industry lobbying kept it approved—the debate continues.

punchline.text: A seaweed extract divides scientists. Safe or harmful? The data disagrees.

quiz.question: What is the key difference in the carrageenan safety debate?
options: Degraded carrageenan causes harm, but food-grade carrageenan is a different molecule
